Wales: Britain's Best-Kept Motorcycling Secret

Wales punches well above its weight for motorcycle riding. Compact enough to cross in a day but packed with mountain passes, coastal roads, and verdant valleys, it offers concentrated brilliance. The roads are quieter than England, the scenery rivals Scotland, and you're never far from a warm welcome and a decent cup of tea.

The Black Mountain Road (A4069)

The A4069 across the Black Mountain in the Brecon Beacons is arguably Wales' finest motorcycle road. Sweeping through open moorland before plunging into tight hairpins, it's been compared to Alpine passes. The surface is generally good and the views across the Towy Valley are spectacular. This road featured in Top Gear and has become a pilgrimage route for petrolheads.

The Evo Triangle

Named by Evo Magazine, the Evo Triangle in North Wales connects the A543, A5, and B4501 in a circuit of stunning roads. The A543 from Denbigh to Pentrefoelas crosses wild moorland, while the A5 through the Ogwen Valley is one of Britain's great driving roads. Complete the loop via the B4501 past Llyn Brenig reservoir.

Snowdonia Passes

Snowdonia offers several outstanding mountain passes:

  • Llanberis Pass (A4086) — Dramatic cliffs and the shadow of Snowdon itself
  • Pen-y-Pass to Capel Curig — Flowing road through the heart of Snowdonia
  • Crimea Pass (A470) — Fast sweepers with mountain panoramas
  • Bwlch y Groes — Wales' highest road pass at 545m, steep and narrow
Wales has more road per square mile than almost anywhere in the UK. The B-roads are where the real adventure lies.

Coastal Roads

The A487 along the Pembrokeshire coast and the roads around the Llyn Peninsula offer beautiful sea views and access to some of Wales' finest beaches. The coast road from Aberystwyth to Machynlleth via the A487 is particularly rewarding, combining mountain and sea views in one ride.

The Valleys

South Wales' valleys are often overlooked but contain some brilliant roads. The A4059 from Aberdare to Brecon climbs through the Cynon Valley and over the Beacons, offering a proper sense of journey. The Gospel Pass above Hay-on-Wye is another hidden gem — a narrow, unfenced road climbing to 549 metres with views into England.

Practical Advice for Riding in Wales

Welsh weather is changeable and the west coast sees significant rainfall. Waterproof gear is essential year-round. Fuel stations are well-spaced in South and mid-Wales but can be scarce in the remote north-west. Many B-roads are single-track with passing places — be prepared to reverse for oncoming traffic. The riding season runs from April to October, with May and September being the sweet spots for dry weather and quiet roads. faq.q: What is the best motorcycle road in Wales?
faq.a: Many riders name the A4069 Black Mountain Road as Wales' finest. It sweeps through open moorland before plunging into tight hairpins with spectacular views across the Towy Valley. The surface is generally good and it featured on Top Gear, so it now draws riders and drivers from across Britain.

faq.q: When should I ride in Wales?
faq.a: The season runs April to October, with May and September the sweet spots for drier weather and quiet roads. Welsh weather is changeable and the west coast sees significant rainfall, so waterproof gear is essential year-round even during the summer months.

faq.q: Are Welsh mountain passes suitable for less experienced riders?
faq.a: The main passes are manageable, but many B-roads are single-track with passing places and you may need to reverse for oncoming traffic. Sheep appear around blind bends without warning and wet tarmac with moss reduces grip, so build confidence on the wider A-roads first.

faq.q: How is fuel availability in Wales?
faq.a: Fuel stations are well spaced in South and mid-Wales but can be scarce in the remote north-west. The valleys are well served, yet stations are rare on the passes themselves, so fill up before climbing into the mountains and never leave a town on a low tank.
